why: A client log upload is opaque bytes. Upstream declares string/binary, which generates a named type the handler cannot convert a []byte to.
An uploaded lyric file is opaque bytes. Same string/binary problem as the client log upload.
A named configuration is a different shape per key, so the response is declared string/binary upstream and has to stay untyped here.
The device profile is forty-odd nested structs describing codecs we do not read. It is accepted opaquely and handed back unchanged.
